business_problem: The bank wanted to manage many offers in real time and deliver highly targeted pricing, incentives, and advice across the customer journey without the delays and risk of its legacy process.
solution_summary: Capgemini helped a leading financial-services institution replace a legacy offer-management process with a real-time, AI-enabled decision and delivery platform. The new architecture uses Naehas as the offer-creation hub, where marketers define products, pricing, eligibility, rules, and content, while Adobe ingests offer data and customer-experience events so personalized offers can be presented across channels as customers move through their journey. Around that core, AI models analyze factors such as age, income, and product-buying patterns to predict the next best product and tailor incentives, advice, and pricing. The implementation also introduced access control, auditability, compliance support, and a single user interface for marketers, turning offer creation, approval, and distribution from a slow manual workflow into a governed, always-on personalization engine.

solution_components.name: Naehas
solution_components.role: Acts as the offer-creation hub where marketers define products, pricing, rules, eligibility, and content for personalized offers.

solution_components.name: Adobe
solution_components.role: Ingests offer data and customer-experience events so personalized offers can be delivered across customer touchpoints.

data_flow: Marketers configure offers, pricing, and eligibility in Naehas, while Adobe ingests offer data and customer-experience events from digital channels. AI analyzes customer attributes and buying patterns to predict next-best offers, and the platform then presents governed personalized offers across the customer journey with auditing and compliance controls in place.
integration_points: Offer data and regulated-content approval workflow
business_outcome: The bank increased personalization and sped up offer creation and approval while lowering operating and IT costs and reducing the risk and friction of regulated-content changes.
metrics: 25% decrease in the risk of errors
